title: Telemetry Sampling Strategy, Cost Signal Retrospective, and 12-Month Roadmap
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This page documents the platform telemetry sampling strategy we adopted in H2 2025 for cost signals and high-cardinality traces, the retrospective results after the first six months, and a practical 12-month roadmap of improvements. It is intended for platform engineers, observability owners, and product teams who rely on accurate cost attribution and latency diagnostics.

Background

- Problem: Our raw telemetry (token-level traces, per-request kernel timings, and tenant-level cost attributions) was growing 2.4x year-over-year. Storage and query costs were rising and dashboards became slower. High-cardinality debug traces in production were noisy and expensive.
- Objective: Reduce telemetry spend while preserving the fidelity required for SLOs, incident investigation, and per-tenant cost allocation.
- Constraints: No lost legal/audit signals, minimal changes to SDKs used by customers, and maintainability by a small oncall team.

Goals and Success Criteria

1. Reduce observability storage cost by 30% in 6 months while keeping investigation time-to-resolution (MTTR) within +/-10% of baseline.
2. Preserve end-to-end unit cost attribution accuracy within 5% for top 80% of customers by spend.
3. Ensure any sampling change is reversible within one rollout window and has clear guardrails documented in the runbook.

Signal Inventory (what we collect today)

- Cost signals: per-request token count, model_variant, quantization_profile, tenant_id, route_id, timestamp, CPU/GPU-time-ms.
- Latency signals: request_latency_ms, tokenize_time_ms, generation_time_ms, kernel_launch_time_ms.
- Traces & spans: request->runtime->kernel spans (high-cardinality when including prompt hash).
- Derived metrics: cost_per_token, percentile latency per model variant, daily spend per tenant.

Problem characterization from the pilot

- 70% of storage growth came from high-cardinality debug traces (prompt hashes and full request bodies).
- 15% came from infrequently queried hourly histograms (we stored raw samples instead of aggregated sketches).
- The top 10 tenants produced 55% of trace volume, but investigation needs were concentrated on 2–3 tenants during incidents.

Design: Adaptive Sampling Tiers

We split telemetry into four sampling tiers to balance cost and fidelity:

- Tier 0 (Full): 100% of data for legal/audit signals, billing pipelines, and SLA metering. No sampling.
- Tier 1 (High fidelity): 10%–100% adaptive for high-variance tenants and routes flagged by anomaly detectors.
- Tier 2 (Statistical): 1%–10% for routine production traffic (sufficient for percentile estimates and cost attribution after normalization).
- Tier 3 (Light): 0.01%–1% for debug traces and request bodies; reserved for rare on-demand troubleshooting.

Rule lattice (decision matrix)

- Always include Tier 0 keys: invoice_id, tenant_id, billing_version.
- Promote a tenant to Tier 1 when 1) %change in spend > 20% week-over-week, or 2) a latency anomaly with p95 > SLO*1.5 is detected.
- Demote a tenant if 7-day variance falls below threshold and no anomalies detected for 14 days.
- Specified routes (e.g., rerank endpoints, model-mix experiments) are tagged to sample at min(Tier setting, route_min).

Implementation details (how-to)

1) Sampling rules configuration (stored in Platform Config Service). Example YAML rule: 

sampling_rules:
  - name: billing-mandatory
    match: 'has(billing_version) && true'
    tier: 0
    reason: 'Audit and billing'

  - name: high-variance-tenant
    match: 'tenant_spend_change_pct > 20'
    tier: 1
    min_rate: 0.1
    max_rate: 1.0
    reason: 'Adaptive promotion for cost/latency anomalies'

  - name: default-production
    match: 'env == "prod"'
    tier: 2
    rate: 0.02
    reason: 'Statistical sampling for cost signals'

  - name: debug-traces
    match: 'tagged_debug == true'
    tier: 3
    rate: 0.0005
    reason: 'On-demand debug traces'

2) SDK/agent behavior
- The telemetry agent computes a deterministic hash over (tenant_id, route_id, time-window) to allow consistent sampling without coordination.
- For Tier 1 promotions the control plane sends short-lived overrides (TTL=24h) to edge agents.
- Promoted traces are kept for 30 days; demoted aggregates are kept as sketches for 90 days.

3) Ingestion & storage changes
- Convert raw per-token histograms into sketches (DDSketch) for long-tail percentiles for Tier 2 signals.
- Persist full traces to hot storage only for Tier 0 and Tier 1. Tier 3 traces are archived to cold storage (30 day retrieval SLA).

Dashboard and alert impacts

- Dashboards must display sampling rate annotations on every panel (top-right badge) and estimated confidence intervals when sampling <5%.
- Alerts using sampled metrics must include a classifier that verifies sampling rate is above the panel-specific threshold before firing; otherwise the alert is suppressed.

PromQL examples

- Estimated p95 adjustment when using sketch-backed histograms: 
  topk(10, quantile_over_time(0.95, request_latency_ms_bucket[7d]))

- Sampling-aware alert: compute effective rate and only alert if above min_rate 
  sample_rate = sum(sampling_weight{route=~".*"}) / sum(requests_total{route=~".*"})
  alert: HighP95IfSampled
  expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) ) > 1.5 * oncall_p95_slo) and (sample_rate > 0.02)

Runbook: Troubleshooting sampling regressions

1. Symptoms
   - sudden gaps in per-tenant spend panels
   - alerts failing to trigger despite increased error rates
   - query timeouts on dashboards with low sampling rate warning

2. Immediate checks (operator steps)
   - Check Platform Config Service for recent sampling_rules changes (audit trail).
   - Query sample_rate by tenant: 
     prod> sum(rate(sampled_requests_total{tenant_id="$TENANT"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{tenant_id="$TENANT"}[5m]))
   - If sample_rate unexpectedly low and change is recent, rollback config by toggling the rule to previous version (Platform Config Service supports quick rollback).

3. Escalation path
   - Pager: eng-platform oncall -> Observability SRE -> API infra owner. Include runbook link and last config diff.

Retrospective: H2 2025 pilot (summary of learnings)

- What we changed: Introduced Tier 2 default 2% sampling for production traces and a promotion policy for top-variance tenants. Converted request histograms to DDSketch for long-tail percentile estimation.
- Measured outcomes (first 6 months):
  - Observability storage cost: -33% (met goal).
  - MTTR: +6% (slower in a few categories where low-sampled traces masked rare failure modes, but still within goal).
  - Billing accuracy (top 80% spend): within 3.2% of baseline.
  - False negatives on anomaly detection rose from 2.1% to 3.8% for very rare events (<0.01% traffic).

- Key root causes for issues encountered:
  - Over-eager demotion logic removed important diagnostic traces during staggered rollout windows.
  - Dashboard queries lacked sampling-awareness and produced misleading percentiles in a handful of panels.
  - Some SDK versions did not implement deterministic hashing correctly; caused sampling drift across edges.

Action items completed in the pilot

- Enforced SDK version gate for production for agents that perform sampling (rollout block until 2.3.1+).
- Added sampling-rate display and CI tests for dashboard panels.
- Implemented TTL-based promotion rules to avoid long tail demotions.

12-month roadmap (priority and owners)

Q1 2026 (done):
- Stabilize deterministic hashing and release SDK 2.4.0 (owner: eng-developer-experience).
- Add sampling rate badges and confidence bands to all runtime-cost dashboards (owner: eng-platform dashboards).

Q2 2026:
- Build a lightweight anomaly sketching service to surface rare signals without full trace retention (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Add automated canary promotions for canary tenants running new models (owner: eng-platform + product).

Q3 2026:
- Integrate sampling rules with the rollout service to automatically prevent demotions during active rollouts (owner: eng-platform).
- Pilot request-body redaction before traces are stored to reduce cardinality while preserving debug value (owner: security-and-compliance).

Q4 2026:
- Evaluate machine-learned sampling policies that prioritize traces based on predicted investigative value (owner: applied-ml-and-evals).
- Migrate Tier 3 cold traces to 7-day hot cache for rapid incident response (owner: eng-infra).

Metrics to track (KPIs)

- Observability spend (cost/month) — target -30% baseline by 2026-06.
- Billing attribution error (top 80%) — target <5% drift.
- MTTR for platform incidents — target within +/-10% of baseline.
- Sampling coverage for top 20 tenants — target >= 5% average per day.

Governance and rollout checklist

1. Create a change request in Platform Config Service with diff and test plan.
2. Run the dashboard CI to surface any panels that become unreliable when sampling_rate < configured threshold.
3. Stage rollout to 10% of tenants for 72 hours; monitor sample_rate and dashboard health.
4. If any of these fail, rollback and create a postmortem.

Appendix: Useful queries, config endpoints, and ownership

- Platform Config Service API: GET /v1/config/sampling_rules, PATCH /v1/config/sampling_rules/{id}/rollback
- Sample rate panels: grafana/dashboard/db/platform-sampling-overview
- Owners: eng-platform (primary), eng-serving-runtime (runtime changes), eng-developer-experience (SDKs), security-and-compliance (PII/redaction)
